note: Track hearing-changes (theory-ear), step 3, on the ear game asked for chord changes (interval-ears, kind change) at its level 2, which adds vi to IV and V: the backing track plays the three changes in C, the minor one first, then the game asks all three in a new key each time. The why gives the method (the 6 is the only minor chord of the four), and the game's text says what to do when the 4 and the 6 get mixed up.

exercise.title: The 6th chord among the 4th and the 5th
exercise.why: The 6th chord is the only minor chord among the 1, 4, 5 and 6, so its minor sound gives it away before you hear how far the chord moved.

cells.text:
Press Play below to start the backing track in C: C and Am take turns, then C and F, then C and G. Watch the lit chord box, and call out 6 on every Am, 4 on every F and 5 on every G.
Am is the only minor chord of the four, so listen for the change where the sound turns minor.

Press Start in the game below to hear two chords: the 1st chord, then the 4, the 5 or the 6, in a new key each time. Pick IV, V or vi: vi is the 6th chord, written small because it is minor.
Press Replay below to hear the two chords again before you pick. Press Next for two new chords.
Practice until the 4 and the 6 no longer get mixed up: when they do, press Replay below and listen for whether the second chord is major or minor.
